title: Frontend: Implement Promise Race
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Implement Promise Race. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement async solution(entries). Each entry has {value,delay,reject?}; start all lazy timer tasks and return {status:fulfilled|rejected,value} for the first settlement. Delays are distinct nonnegative integers. Empty entries return {status:pending} as an observable model of an unsettled race.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Return a promise and attach fulfillment/rejection handlers through Promise.resolve for each iterable item.
alternativeApproaches: Contrast race with any and explain why winning a race does not cancel losing operations.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Immediate value; first rejection; empty iterable.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
